answer: Every agent identity is minted in an onyx vault, bound to one hardware key and a bonded sponsor. The network runs one pulse check: peers must attest within a short window, and each attestation carries staked deposits. A sybil swarm of fake identities owns no collateral, so when a clone misattests, slashing burns the deposit and marks the whole swarm. Over time trust settles into shale layers — fresh agents carry little weight, long-attested agents anchor consensus, and cloning an identity becomes an economic loss instead of a free ride.
